fullPassage: At the spring picnic held at the community center, Eleanor sat quietly at a table. Around her, people laughed and chatted, but she felt out of place. Large groups had always made her nervous. Then, Martha, a friendly newcomer, introduced herself to Eleanor and reassured her that things would get easier. By the end of the picnic, Martha had convinced Eleanor to join her at a pottery class the following week. Eleanor hesitated but eventually agreed. At the pottery class, Eleanor's nerves returned. She stared at the lump of clay in front of her, unsure of where to begin. Martha, sitting next to her, offered a reassuring smile. "Don't worry about being perfect," she said. Eleanor nodded and began shaping the clay. When Martha's pot collapsed into a funny, lopsided shape, she burst out laughing. Eleanor couldn't control herself, and she joined in, her tension easing. By the end of the class, Eleanor had managed to create a small, sturdy bowl. "That's beautiful!" Martha exclaimed, admiring Eleanor's work. "You're a natural." Eleanor smiled, feeling a spark of pride. She said that she might come back the following week. As their friendship grew, Martha encouraged Eleanor to try new activities. They joined a hiking group, and Eleanor found herself enjoying the fresh air and exercise. And one day, Martha suggested kayaking at the local lake. On a bright Saturday morning, they found themselves sitting in a tandem kayak, paddles in hand. The first few minutes were wobbly as they tried to coordinate their movements, but soon they found a rhythm. Gliding across the calm lake, Eleanor felt a rush of excitement she hadn't felt in years. By the end of the summer, Eleanor felt like a new person. She was no longer the shy woman who had sat alone at the picnic. Her friendship with Martha had opened doors she hadn't thought possible.

questions.passage: At the spring picnic held at the community center, Eleanor sat quietly at a table. Around her, people laughed and chatted, but she felt out of place. Large groups had always made her nervous. Then, Martha, a friendly newcomer, introduced herself to Eleanor and reassured her that things would get easier. By the end of the picnic, Martha had convinced Eleanor to join her at a pottery class the following week. Eleanor hesitated but eventually agreed. At the pottery class, Eleanor's nerves returned. She stared at the lump of clay in front of her, unsure of where to begin. Martha, sitting next to her, offered a reassuring smile. "Don't worry about being perfect," she said. Eleanor nodded and began shaping the clay. When Martha's pot collapsed into a funny, lopsided shape, she burst out laughing. Eleanor couldn't control herself, and she joined in, her tension easing. By the end of the class, Eleanor had managed to create a small, sturdy bowl. "That's beautiful!" Martha exclaimed, admiring Eleanor's work. "You're a natural." Eleanor smiled, feeling a spark of pride. She said that she might come back the following week. As their friendship grew, Martha encouraged Eleanor to try new activities. They joined a hiking group, and Eleanor found herself enjoying the fresh air and exercise. And one day, Martha suggested kayaking at the local lake. On a bright Saturday morning, they found themselves sitting in a tandem kayak, paddles in hand. The first few minutes were wobbly as they tried to coordinate their movements, but soon they found a rhythm. Gliding across the calm lake, Eleanor felt a rush of excitement she hadn't felt in years. By the end of the summer, Eleanor felt like a new person. She was no longer the shy woman who had sat alone at the picnic. Her friendship with Martha had opened doors she hadn't thought possible.
